clue.text: Is probing male's first and foremost injury

indicators.note: something probing goes into what it explores, so the first word sits inside the rest

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for male; the 's just joins it to what follows
chief means principal, first and foremost in rank

explanation.surface: A doctor asks about the man's main injury, as if prodding the wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and foremost' looks like an instruction to take initial letters, but it is one synonym for CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief in its older sense means harm or damage done to someone.

clue.text: Firing international, into gin unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drinker reports an international incident: someone fell into the gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges INTO GIN to give GNITION, placed after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignition is the setting alight or firing of fuel, as in an engine.

clue.text: Cold, and beginning to feel stiff

indicators.note: the beginning of the word that follows means just its first letter

parts.note: stiff and rigid both mean unable to bend

explanation.surface: Someone describes going numb and stiff in freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid is a formal synonym for very cold, as in frigid Arctic air.

clue.text: Member of the clergy reportedly shot playing billiards

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for the churchman is wanted by its sound

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A cleric is said to have been shot during a game of billiards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'shot' a shooting; it is a stroke at billiards.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a cannon is a stroke where the cue ball strikes two other balls in turn.

clue.text: Makes an idiotic error, initially, supplying homonym

indicators.note: something idiotic is senseless, signalling the letters are put into a new order
initially means take only the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone blunders badly at the start, then offers a word that sounds like another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'idiotic' looks like it describes the error, but it rearranges MAKES AN into NAMESAK, before E.
explanation.definitionFit: A homonym can mean a person bearing the same name as another, just as a namesake does.

clue.text: Will a drink from this give you courage?

definitions.text: Will a drink from this give you courage?

parts.words: Will a drink from this give you courage?
parts.note: the vessel holding a drink is also British slang for nerve, so 'Dutch courage' links both senses

explanation.surface: A nervous person wonders if a stiff drink will calm their nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, having the BOTTLE means having nerve; it is also the container a drink is poured from.
explanation.definitionFit: The glass container holds drink, and British slang uses the same word for nerve or guts.

clue.text: I, with knight, greet by arrangement a whole number

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: by arrangement means the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A man meets a knight and says hello as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knight' is N, as in chess notation; 'by arrangement' is the signal to rearrange 'greet'.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a number with no fractional part, such as 7 or minus 3.

clue.text: Feature some extra items

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An advert boasts that a product includes a few additional extras.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or characteristic of a person or thing.

clue.text: Swagger of a daughter in good show!

indicators.note: in says the letters go inside the exclamation

parts.note: bravo is a cry of approval, like good show!

explanation.surface: A proud parent swaggers as their daughter puts on a fine performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness meant to impress, much like swagger.

clue.text: Sleep so long with son

parts.note: so long and bye-bye are both casual farewells

explanation.surface: A parent tells a boy to sleep and says goodnight.
explanation.walkthrough: Bye-byes is a nursery word for sleep, as in going to bye-byes.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's talk for going to bed and sleeping, as in time for nap time.

clue.text: Film one omnivorous creature

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or coat, as of dust or paint
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A documentary is announced about one animal that eats everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie; it is a thin layer, a COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a South American relative of the raccoon that eats both plants and small animals.

clue.text: Area in which there may be no developments?

definitions.text: Area in which there may be no developments?

parts.words: Area in which there may be no developments?
parts.note: developments here means housing building, banned in protected countryside around British towns

explanation.surface: Someone asks where nothing new ever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developments' reads as news or progress, but means building projects; a green belt is protected open land ringing a British town.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning law in Britain forbids most building on the protected rural ring around cities.

clue.text: DIY ads then, again recollected just now

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remembers old do-it-yourself adverts being shown once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembered; read as re-collected it scrambles the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present era, nowadays, at the current moment.

clue.text: Fine lines about Stuart monarch, or flattery?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the lines go round the monarch

parts.note: L is short for line, so two of them give LL
Queen Anne was the last monarch of the House of Stuart

explanation.surface: A courtier pens elegant verses about Queen Anne, sincere or sycophantic.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage this word means smooth talk or flattery, as well as a washcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally in Britain it means smooth, insincere talk meant to please or evade.

clue.text: Everyone at home welcoming a church marriage

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the a goes inside

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The whole family gathers at home to welcome a church wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union, especially one formed by marriage between families.

clue.text: Type of delivery members nail

parts.note: legs are limbs, members of the body
to pin is to fasten, like nail

explanation.surface: A carpenter's delivery of supplies includes components and nails.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a leg-spin delivery is a ball the bowler spins from leg to off.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler's delivery can be of the wrist-spun kind that turns from the leg side.

clue.text: Wise having drain that is not emptied?

parts.note: to sap is to drain energy or strength
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is clever to have a drain that never empties.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a literary word for wise or knowing.

clue.text: Confident attitude about current ITV broadcast

indicators.note: about means around, so the pose surrounds the rest

parts.note: an attitude can mean a posture or pose
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV executive has an upbeat view of ITV's latest show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns ITV into TIV; ITV is a British commercial television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Positive can mean certain or sure, just as confident does.

clue.text: Illegally enter hydro, breaking lock

indicators.note: breaking into means getting inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a hydro is a British spa hotel offering water treatments

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks the lock to enter a health resort illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door; it is a lock of hair. A hydro is a British health spa hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to go onto land or property without permission.

clue.text: Tricking, slyly, all up feasting on bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Monkeys trick their keepers, gorging on bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the food being eaten; it is slang for crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for deceiving someone craftily, getting one over on them.

clue.text: Miserable, friend on trial

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a try is a trial or attempt

explanation.surface: A friend's court case leaves them wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' suggests a court; it is an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means meagre or worthless, as in a miserable sum.

clue.text: One after the other having an argument

definitions.meaning: quarrelling, from row meaning a noisy dispute

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way the phrase means consecutively; read with row as quarrel it means arguing.

clue.text: Knocks down storeys

definitions.meaning: fells someone with a blow, as a boxer does

explanation.surface: A demolition crew brings a building down level by level.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means knocks to the ground; as a noun, the levels of a building.

clue.text: Ordinary circuit breaker may be helpful

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
a fuse breaks an electric circuit when overloaded

explanation.surface: An electrician suggests a standard circuit breaker might come in handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable that helps is said to be worth using, so useful.

clue.text: Dog has a drink taken outside, accordingly

indicators.note: taken outside means the drink is put around the other words

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a dog laps water
so means therefore, accordingly

explanation.surface: A dog has a drink outdoors, as one would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small long-haired Tibetan breed of dog.

clue.text: Top seat taken by head of table

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: seat can mean the backside, the rump

explanation.surface: A diner takes the place at the end of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' looks like a chair; it is the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump is to outdo or beat, as when topping a rival's offer.

clue.text: Heading off Moroccan wild animal

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the remaining letters are rearranged
heading off means the first letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A wild beast from Morocco runs off into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' removes M from MOROCCAN; 'wild' rearranges OROCCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringtailed, masked North American mammal is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Critical assessments concerning convictions

parts.note: re means concerning, about
convictions are firmly held views or beliefs

explanation.surface: Reviewers judge someone's firmly held beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convictions' suggests court verdicts; it means beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics write reviews, which are evaluations of a book, play or film.
